titulo: European Telescope Discovers ‘Einstein Ring’ in Nearby Galaxy

fuente.licencia: Dominio público (VOA, gobierno de EE. UU.)
fuente.nota: Text shortened by removing paragraphs; the sentences are unchanged.

parrafos: Scientists say Europe’s Euclid space telescope has discovered a bright ring of light circling a nearby galaxy. The observed light is known as an Einstein ring.
Researchers have estimated the ring encircles a galaxy 590 million light years away from Earth. A light year is the distance light travels in a year – about 9.5 trillion kilometers.
Astronomers have long known about the galaxy where the ring was discovered. So, they were surprised that the bright ring had not been identified before.
Einstein rings are rare. They form when light from a more distant galaxy bends around a closer galaxy. The nearer galaxy appears to have a circle of light, or a halo, around it.
The Einstein ring gets its name from physicist Albert Einstein. Einstein predicted that light would bend around extremely massive objects in space. This is called “gravitational lensing.”

The American space agency NASA explains that as light passes through a gravitational lens, “it may take different paths, producing multiple images of the same object.” In this way, gravity itself acts as a lens, magnifying and distorting space and time in a way that is similar to an optical lens like those in eyeglasses or contact lenses.

Gravitational lenses permit telescopes like Euclid to observe more distant and less-bright objects. In the latest project, researchers from Germany’s Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics used data from Euclid to create a computer model to discover the Einstein ring.

The Euclid space telescope is operated by the European Space Agency (ESA). In 2023, it launched on a six-year mission that ESA officials have said aims to study the mysteries of dark matter and dark energy across the universe.

Astronomers at the Max Planck Institute are leading the research. In a statement, the organization said the first sign that the Einstein ring existed came during testing right after Euclid was deployed. A team member, Bruno Altieri, was looking over early data collected by Euclid.

“Even from that first observation, I could see it,” Altieri said in a statement. “But after Euclid made more observations of the area, we could see a perfect Einstein ring. For me, with a lifelong interest in gravitational lensing, that was amazing.”

The scientists said the more distant galaxy involved in the method is about 4.4 billion light years away from Earth. They noted that the more distant galaxy had never been observed before and does not have a name.

Conor O’Riordan is another team member from the Max Planck Institute and was the lead writer of the study. He said, “All strong lenses are special, because they're so rare, and they're incredibly useful scientifically. This one is particularly special, because it’s so close to Earth and the alignment makes it very beautiful.”

O’Riordan added that the researchers used the latest gravitational lensing methods developed at the institute. This permitted them to model the light of the ring. “We even had to look at some of the raw data to better understand how the detector works.”

O’Riordan said the team’s modeling operations were just the first step in studying the newly discovered Einstein ring. He said the group plans to use the ring to also study “dark matter substructures” within the lensing galaxy.
Bryan Lynn wrote this story for VOA Learning English, based on reports from The Associated Press, the Max Planck Institute, the European Space Agency and NASA.
titulo_es: A European telescope discovers an “Einstein ring” in a nearby galaxy
resumen_es: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has detected an Einstein ring around a nearby galaxy; the text explains the phenomenon of gravitational lensing and the role of the researchers at the Max Planck Institute.
nivel_motivo: The vocabulary level rises because of the astronomical terms, which the text itself explains; the syntax is simple and typical of an adapted text, so it fits B2.

ideas_clave.idea: Europe's Euclid space telescope has spotted an Einstein ring, a bright circle of light around a galaxy about 590 million light years away.
Scientists were surprised, because the galaxy had long been known but the ring had gone unnoticed.
Such rings are rare and appear when the light of a farther galaxy is bent by a nearer, very massive one, a phenomenon Einstein predicted and known as gravitational lensing.
Gravitational lenses help telescopes see faint, distant objects; Euclid, run by ESA and launched in 2023, is on a six-year mission to study dark matter and dark energy.
Bruno Altieri of the Max Planck Institute noticed the ring in Euclid's earliest test data, and later observations revealed it clearly.
The background galaxy, 4.4 billion light years away, had never been seen before, and the lead author stresses how rare, useful and beautiful this nearby lens is.
The team modelled the ring with new lensing techniques and now plans to use it to investigate dark matter within the foreground galaxy, as reported by VOA.

resumen_modelo: The text reports that the European Space Agency's Euclid telescope has detected an Einstein ring around a galaxy some 590 million light years from Earth. Although this galaxy had been known for a long time, the ring had never been noticed before. Such rings, which are rare, form when the light of a more distant galaxy is bent by the gravity of a closer one, a phenomenon called gravitational lensing that Albert Einstein had predicted. Gravity thus acts like an optical lens, allowing telescopes to observe faint and remote objects. Euclid, launched in 2023 to investigate dark matter and dark energy, revealed the ring in its very first test data. The scientists stress that this lens is especially valuable because it is so close to Earth, and they intend to use it to study dark matter.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: A light year is a unit of time equal to one year.
preguntas.cita: A light year is the distance light travels in a year – about 9.5 trillion kilometers.
preguntas.explicacion: A light year is a unit of distance, not of time: the distance light travels in a year, about 9.5 trillion kilometres.

preguntas.pregunta: Why were astronomers surprised by the discovery?
opciones: Because the galaxy had never been observed before
Because the galaxy was well known but the ring had not been identified
Because Einstein rings were thought not to exist
Because the ring was very far from Earth
respuestas: Because the galaxy was well known but the ring had not been identified
preguntas.cita: Astronomers have long known about the galaxy where the ring was discovered. So, they were surprised that the bright ring had not been identified before.
preguntas.explicacion: The surprise is that the galaxy had been known for a long time. The galaxy never observed before is the more distant one; rings are rare, but they were known to exist, and the text stresses precisely how close this one is.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 3 a word that means “a circle of light around an object”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning 'a circle of light around an object'.
preguntas.cita: The nearer galaxy appears to have a circle of light, or a halo, around it.
preguntas.explicacion: A “halo” is a ring of light (es: halo, aureola); the text presents it as a synonym of “circle of light”.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: Einstein predicted that light would bend around extremely massive objects.
preguntas.cita: Einstein predicted that light would bend around extremely massive objects in space.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says so; the phenomenon is called gravitational lensing and gives the ring its name.

preguntas.pregunta: According to NASA, what can happen when light passes through a gravitational lens?
opciones: It may produce multiple images of the same object
respuestas: It may produce multiple images of the same object
preguntas.cita: it may take different paths, producing multiple images of the same object
preguntas.explicacion: Light can follow different paths and produce several images of the same object. The other options do not appear in the text and contradict the idea that gravity acts as a lens.

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 5 a word that means “increasing the apparent size”.
preguntas.pregunta: Find a word meaning 'making something look bigger'.
preguntas.cita: gravity itself acts as a lens, magnifying and distorting space and time
preguntas.explicacion: “To magnify” means to make something look bigger; hence “magnifying glass”. It does not mean “magnificar” in the sense of exaggerating.

opciones: To search for life on other planets
To study dark matter and dark energy
To map the surface of the Moon
To test Einstein's theory of relativity
respuestas: To study dark matter and dark energy
preguntas.cita: aims to study the mysteries of dark matter and dark energy across the universe
preguntas.explicacion: The six-year mission aims to study dark matter and dark energy. The other options are not mentioned as goals of Euclid.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: The first sign of the ring appeared several years after Euclid was deployed.

preguntas.explicacion: The first sign appeared during testing, just after deployment, not years later.

preguntas.pregunta: Why was the discovery particularly exciting for Bruno Altieri?
respuestas: Because he had been interested in gravitational lensing all his life, and he could already see the ring in Euclid's first observation; later observations confirmed it was a perfect Einstein ring.
preguntas.cita: For me, with a lifelong interest in gravitational lensing, that was amazing.
preguntas.explicacion: The answer must mention her lifelong interest in gravitational lenses and the fact that she saw the ring from the very first observation.

preguntas.enunciado: Say whether the statement is true, false or not stated in the text.
preguntas.pregunta: The scientists have decided to name the distant galaxy after Bruno Altieri.
preguntas.explicacion: The text says the distant galaxy has no name, but it does not mention any plan to give it one.

preguntas.pregunta: According to Conor O'Riordan, what makes this lens particularly special?
respuestas: All strong lenses are rare and scientifically valuable, but this one stands out because it is very close to Earth and its alignment makes it especially beautiful.
preguntas.cita: This one is particularly special, because it’s so close to Earth and the alignment makes it very beautiful.
preguntas.explicacion: You need to distinguish what applies to all strong lenses (rarity, usefulness) from what is specific to this one (closeness and alignment).

preguntas.enunciado: Find in paragraph 12 an expression that means “unprocessed data”.
preguntas.cita: We even had to look at some of the raw data to better understand how the detector works.
preguntas.explicacion: “Raw data” are data that have not been processed; “raw” also means uncooked (es: crudo).

preguntas.pregunta: What does the team plan to do next with the Einstein ring?
opciones: Study dark matter substructures in the lensing galaxy
Send a new telescope to observe it
Stop the research because the modeling is finished
respuestas: Study dark matter substructures in the lensing galaxy
preguntas.cita: the group plans to use the ring to also study “dark matter substructures” within the lensing galaxy
preguntas.explicacion: The next step is to study dark matter substructures. Modelling is only “the first step”, and naming the galaxy or a new telescope is not mentioned.
